pharm: Intracellular inhibitor of PDGFR, FGFR, and VEGFR tyrosine kinases
quick: 150 mg orally twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart, with food
Can cause fetal harm; effective contraception required during and for >=3 months after
No adjustment for mild-moderate; not studied in severe (CrCl <30) / ESRD
Mild (Child-Pugh A): 100 mg twice daily; NOT recommended in moderate-severe (Child-Pugh B/C)
Avoid heavy use (additive hepatotoxicity / GI effects)
Liver function tests (baseline then periodic), pregnancy test in females, signs of bleeding/MI/GI perforation
summary: Nintedanib is an oral antifibrotic tyrosine kinase inhibitor for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), chronic fibrosing interstitial lung diseases with a progressive phenotype, and systemic sclerosis-associated ILD. The standard dose is 150 mg twice daily with food. Key risks include hepatotoxicity/drug-induced liver injury, GI effects (notably diarrhea), embryo-fetal toxicity, arterial thromboembolism, bleeding, and GI perforation.
indications: Chronic fibrosing interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) with a progressive phenotype
Slowing the rate of decline in pulmonary function in systemic sclerosis-associated ILD (SSc-ILD)

dosage.t: Approximately 12 hours apart, taken with food
dosage.n: Consider temporary reduction to 100 mg twice daily, interruption, or discontinuation to manage adverse reactions

admin: Take capsules whole with food and liquid; do not chew or crush
Conduct liver function tests and a pregnancy test (females of reproductive potential) before initiation
Manage adverse reactions with dose reduction to 100 mg twice daily, interruption, or discontinuation
moa: Nintedanib is a small-molecule inhibitor of multiple receptor tyrosine kinases - platelet-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) alpha/beta, fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) 1-3, and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR) 1-3 - and certain non-receptor kinases, blocking signaling pathways involved in fibroblast proliferation, migration, and the fibrotic process.

absolute: None per FDA label (no contraindications listed)
relative: Moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B/C) - not recommended
Recent abdominal surgery / GI perforation risk
Recent arterial thromboembolic event / cardiovascular risk

preg: Based on animal studies and mechanism of action, nintedanib can cause fetal harm. Females of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months after the last dose; oral hormonal contraceptives may be ineffective if vomiting/diarrhea occurs, so a barrier method is advised.
lact: Advise women not to breastfeed during treatment with nintedanib because of potential serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants.
renal: No dose adjustment required for mild-to-moderate renal impairment. Safety/efficacy not studied in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) or end-stage renal disease.
hepatic: For mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A), reduce dose to 100 mg twice daily. Nintedanib is NOT recommended in moderate or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B or C). Elevated liver enzymes and drug-induced liver injury are labeled risks - monitor LFTs.

major: P-glycoprotein inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, erythromycin) - increase nintedanib exposure; monitor for toxicity
P-gp inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John's Wort) - decrease exposure; avoid
interactions.food: Take with food (improves tolerability/exposure); avoid grapefruit (P-gp/CYP effects)
interactions.alcohol: Avoid heavy use - additive hepatotoxicity and GI effects
interactions.diagnostics: Baseline and periodic LFTs; pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential

monitoring: Liver function tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin) at baseline, then periodically (e.g., monthly for 3 months, then every 3 months)
Pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential before initiation
Signs/symptoms of bleeding, GI perforation, and cardiovascular events
counsel: Always take with food, about 12 hours apart, and swallow capsules whole
Diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting are common - report severe or persistent symptoms and stay hydrated
Report dark urine, yellow eyes/skin, severe abdominal pain, chest pain, or unusual bleeding promptly
Use effective contraception (and a barrier method if vomiting/diarrhea); do not breastfeed
Do not stop or change the dose without medical advice
pk: Antifibrotic effect (slowing FVC decline) seen over months
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect from moisture; keep in original blister
pearls: Diarrhea is the dominant adverse effect - manage with hydration, antidiarrheals (e.g., loperamide), and dose reduction to 100 mg twice daily before considering discontinuation.
Embryo-fetal toxicity warning: hormonal contraceptives can fail if GI side effects occur, so advise an additional barrier method.
Not recommended in moderate/severe hepatic impairment; reduce to 100 mg BID in mild (Child-Pugh A) impairment.
As an antiangiogenic kinase inhibitor it shares class risks: bleeding, arterial thromboembolism, and GI perforation - withhold around major surgery.
missed: If a dose is missed, take the next dose at the next scheduled time. Do not make up the missed dose and do not exceed the recommended maximum daily dose.
overdose: No specific antidote or treatment for overdose. Based on the safety profile, overdose may worsen GI and hepatic adverse effects. Discontinue and provide supportive care with monitoring of liver function.
